page: Google Cloud Platform a2-ultragpu-1g is an accelerator-optimized server configured with an Intel Xeon x86_64 CPU providing 12 vCPUs across 6 physical cores at a clock speed of 2.2 GHz. The system features 170.0 GB of system memory, yielding 14.17 GB per core. Acceleration is driven by a single NVIDIA Ampere A100 GPU equipped with 80 GB of VRAM. Local storage is provided by a 402 GB NVMe SSD.

Benchmark data highlights a clear performance tradeoff. The server exhibits top-tier performance in large language model inference tasks, achieving 499.41 tokens per second for prompt processing and 24.47 tokens per second for text generation on a large 70B model. Conversely, general-purpose CPU compute capabilities are relatively limited. Single-core CPU benchmarks, such as stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core, fall into the bottom 25% tier. Multi-core CPU performance, memory bandwidth, and database operations reside in the middle 50% tier.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the hardware allocation is heavily weighted toward GPU-accelerated tasks rather than general-purpose compute density. The high ratio of system memory and dedicated GPU VRAM makes this instance suitable for deep learning, large language model inference, and data science workloads that require substantial accelerator memory, while general-purpose tasks like text processing or single-threaded decompression are less optimal.
description: Google Cloud Platform a2-ultragpu-1g is an accelerator-optimized server designed for GPU-intensive workloads. It features an Intel Xeon x86_64 CPU with 12 vCPUs, 170.0 GB of system memory, a 402 GB local NVMe SSD, and a single NVIDIA Ampere A100 GPU with 80 GB of VRAM. Performance benchmarks demonstrate a significant contrast between CPU and GPU capabilities. The server achieves top-tier results in large language model inference, processing 499.41 tokens per second for prompt processing on a 70B model. However, its single-core CPU performance and single-threaded decompression tasks fall into the bottom 25% tier. Multi-core CPU operations and memory bandwidth perform in the middle 50% tier. This hardware profile is highly optimized for deep learning, LLM inference, and parallelized accelerator tasks, whereas general-purpose single-threaded processing represents a primary tradeoff.
